rav-achai.name: Rav Aḥai
rav-achai.era: Late Amora or early Savora · Babylonia, 5th–6th century
rav-achai.bio: Babylonian sage whose challenges, introduced with “Rav Aḥai refutes,” appear in a few places in the Talmud; tradition often identifies him with the early Savora Rav Aḥai.
rav-achai.prompt: A keen-eyed Babylonian scholar in his 50s with a trimmed dark beard flecked with grey and a sharp, probing expression, one finger raised as if pressing an objection; background of mudbrick academy walls and oil lamps.

rav-acha-brei-derava.name: Rav Aḥa son of Rava
rav-acha-brei-derava.bio: Babylonian Amora of Rav Ashi’s generation who often puts questions to Rav Ashi in the Talmud.
rav-acha-brei-derava.prompt: An earnest Babylonian scholar in his 40s with a short brown beard and an inquiring look, leaning forward as if asking his teacher a question; background of palm groves along the Euphrates at dusk.

shimon-haamasoni.name: Shimon HaAmasoni
shimon-haamasoni.bio: Tanna who expounded every “et” in the Torah until he reached “You shall fear the Lord your God”; elsewhere (Pesaḥim 22b) he is also called Neḥemya HaAmasoni.
shimon-haamasoni.prompt: A humble, reverent scholar in his 60s with a long grey beard and gentle, searching eyes, an open Torah scroll before him; background of a Judean limestone study hall in soft lamplight.
